handoff.reason: Case report of lycopenaemia (excess dietary lycopene intake causing skin/serum discoloration) -- safety signal for high-dose/long-term lycopene intake, not an efficacy record.

identity_notes: Lycopene's retrieval set is dominated by a huge body of OBSERVATIONAL literature (prospective cohorts, case-control studies, Mendelian randomization, cross-sectional/NHANES analyses, and reviews explicitly restricted to 'dietary intake' or 'circulating' lycopene) that measures lycopene as a biomarker of intake or genetic exposure rather than as an administered intervention -- all rejected not_intervention. A second large cluster is agricultural/horticultural tomato-crop science (pest management, fertilization, genetics, pesticide residues) and animal/in-vitro mechanistic studies (rats, pigs, hens, mice, human-derived cell lines), rejected off_topic/animal_or_invitro. Among genuine human oral intervention trials, lycopene is frequently delivered as whole tomato/watermelon food products (juice, sauce, paste) rather than as an isolated capsule, which is appropriate to this identity but means 'oral supplement' claims often reflect a food matrix; these are flagged exact_match when lycopene is the named/measured active, and related_form_differs when it is one of several actives in a combined product (mixed-carotenoid blends, lycopene+arginine/vitamin/selenium combinations, lactolycopene or lycosome-formulated proprietary forms). A recurring route nuance is in oral-mucosal-lesion trials (oral leukoplakia, oral lichen planus, oral submucous fibrosis): most use genuinely oral (swallowed) lycopene capsules and were kept, but some OSMF trials also test intralesional injection or topical gel forms in comparator arms within the same study, flagged accordingly, and topical creams/gels/mouth sprays for skin or xerostomia were rejected not_this_route. The strongest, most consistent efficacy signals across clean single-ingredient RCTs are modest cardiovascular/endothelial effects (21194693, 40936452, 28129549 meta-analysis) and reductions in UV/skin oxidative markers (30836363, 36606553 meta-analysis), while prostate-cancer PSA evidence is predominantly null at the RCT/meta-analysis level (27406859, 35031434) despite a large positive observational-epidemiology literature (rejected here as not_intervention). Bioavailability/pharmacokinetic studies (food matrix, cooking method, co-ingested fat/black pepper) were kept as mechanistic evidence since they directly test lycopene absorption, per the pattern used for other identities.
